[Date]

Aetna Appeals Department  
[Address on the EOB or denial letter]

Re: Appeal of adverse benefit determination  
Member: Morgan Grant  
Member ID: W585722922  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA, Massachusetts  
Reference number: POC-8EE886247D-14307  
Requested service: Unicompartmental/partial knee arthroplasty  
CPT: 27446  
Denial date: August 7, 2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446, partial knee replacement. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. Please reverse the denial and authorize the requested surgery based on the clinical evidence summarized below.

Aetna’s publicly available Knee Arthroplasty Clinical Policy Bulletin, policy number 0660, states that unicompartmental knee arthroplasty may be medically necessary when advanced osteoarthritis affects only one compartment and the member has pain and functional disability, appropriate examination findings, qualifying imaging, and unsuccessful conservative treatment.

The available records address the relevant criteria as follows:

1. Single-compartment, advanced osteoarthritis  
The July 6, 2026 MRI documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition. The imaging documents Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis in the medial compartment. This supports advanced disease affecting a single compartment.

2. Pain and functional disability  
Morgan has had nine months of progressive knee pain despite rest. The pain prevents climbing stairs without assistance and causes awakening three to four times each night. These limitations demonstrate substantial functional impairment.

3. Examination findings  
The examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

4. Conservative treatment  
Morgan used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief. Morgan also received a corticosteroid injection on May 25, 2026, which provided only two weeks of partial relief. Morgan completed 16 supervised physical-therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 12 through July 7, 2026, focusing on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this treatment.

The policy states: “History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy.”

The policy also states: “Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint.”

The MRI documents medial-compartment bone-on-bone disease, and the records document failure of medication, injection, and supervised physical therapy. In light of the severity of the medial-compartment disease, please determine whether the policy’s bone-on-bone exception applies. If Aetna believes that the records do not establish a required duration of conservative therapy, please identify that specific criterion and explain why the documented six months of NSAID treatment, failed injection, and supervised physical therapy do not satisfy or qualify under the applicable policy.

5. Contraindications and risk factors  
The records document no active infection, BMI 29, and no smoking. There is no documented untreated substance use. Please review the complete surgical and clinical records for the remaining policy requirements, including ligament stability, knee arc of motion, deformity, subluxation, inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy, bone loss, and other contraindications. If any of these items are considered missing rather than unsatisfied, please allow submission of supplemental records rather than upholding the denial on an unspecified basis.

Please provide a complete explanation of the denial, including the exact criterion or criteria Aetna determined were not met, the clinical records reviewed, and the version of policy 0660 or any additional clinical-review criteria applied to this request. The denial notice refers generally to medical necessity but does not identify the specific unmet requirement.

I request a full internal appeal and authorization for CPT 27446. Please send the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Morgan Grant  
Member ID: W585722922
